derivations.Haar: Accept x with probability (sqrt3/2)/sqrt(1-x^2), y=y0/u. Accepted x density proportional1/y0 and conditional y density y0/y^2 produce dxdy/y^2; uniform angle supplies the Haar fiber. Separate Monte Carlo assumption and interval numerical error.
derivations.Picard: Uniform multiset law: iid ordered draws weight n!/product m!, reciprocal acceptance product m!/n! equalizes multisets. Effective divisor partitions weighted product binom(A_d+n_d-1,n_d) are uniform. A degree-g Picard class has (p^l-1)/(p-1) effective representatives; reciprocal rejection makes classes uniform because RR ensures all degree-g classes have a representative.
derivations.projection: For J=N^e*c,gcd(c,N)=1, [c] sends Jac into exponent dividing N^e while preserving input N-order. Rows may be reduced only modulo N^e. If norm-arm hypotheses hold, T=pi^* [h_E] pi_* maps into N-torsion and preserves transported input up to nonzero h_E*d. All relations/costs remain explicit.
derivations.source_logic: A structural decomposition of algebraic groups supplies neither an exclusive finite-map partition nor an algorithmic lower bound. An upper bound for one Jacobian algorithm cannot certify a lower bound for all destination algorithms. Corrected finite tests retain avenues for constructive leads.
